# Use cases and triggers — link and recall

Define use cases, how to trigger them, and what to link to so the agent can **recall** the right flow or skill.

**Recall:** When the user’s goal or phrasing matches a use case below, **link** to the listed flow/skill/doc and **run** the superpowers or config flow as specified.

---

## 1. Creative / feature work (idea → done) — **superpowers**

| | |
|--|--|
| **Use case** | User has an idea, feature, or multi-step change; wants to go from idea to done and reviewed. |
| **Trigger** | “I have an idea,” “build a feature,” “add X,” “implement Y,” “run superpowers,” “plan before code,” “brainstorm then implement,” or any non-trivial creative/implementation ask. |
| **Link / recall** | **cursor-workflow-bootstrap**; LOGIC_FLOWS §2, §8, §10. **You have superpowers to run.** |
| **Run** | **brainstorming** → design doc → **writing-plans** → plan doc → **executing-plans** (or **subagent-driven-development**) → **finishing-a-development-branch** → **code-reviewer** + requesting/receiving-code-review. Use **using-cursor-skills** so applicable skills are applied. |

---

## 2. Config or content (add/change skill, agent, rule, settings)

| | |
|--|--|
| **Use case** | User wants to add or change a skill, subagent, rule, slash command, editor settings, or narrative doc; or migrate rules/commands to skills. |
| **Trigger** | “Create a skill,” “add a subagent,” “new rule,” “migrate rules to skills,” “change theme/font/settings,” “port from Claude/Codex,” “/create-skill,” “/create-subagent,” “/migrate-to-skills,” “/update-cursor-settings,” “/cursor-integration,” “/create-rule.” |
| **Link / recall** | **cursor-config-content-workflow**; LOGIC_FLOWS §1, §5; reference-resources-inventory (Config & content creation skills). |
| **Run** | Route once → invoke exactly one skill: create-skill, create-subagent, create-rule, migrate-to-skills, update-cursor-settings, cursor-integration, or narrative-blueprints. |

---

## 3. Analyze / sort / organize a batch of artifacts (zips, paths, lists)

# paste-mcp

Local **MCP app** (tools + picker widget) in front of [Paste](https://pasteapp.io)’s built-in MCP. One widget, two tools: pick a clipboard item, or pick a pinboard. Previews redact API-key-shaped strings. This is not the official Paste server (`pasteapp/paste-mcp`).

## Why a widget

Clipboard history is a long list the model should not dump or rank blindly. A picker is the right surface. Hosts without the apps UI still get the same JSON.

## Run

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # optional
npm install
npm start
```

Default: `http://127.0.0.1:3847/mcp` → talks to Paste at `PASTE_MCP_URL` (`http://127.0.0.1:39725/mcp`). Paste must be running with MCP enabled.

Cursor `mcp.json` (stdio wrapper for widget capability negotiation):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "paste-mcp-app": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "http://127.0.0.1:3847/mcp",
        "--allow-http",
        "--transport",
        "http-only"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Or point `url` at `http://127.0.0.1:3847/mcp` the same way as the official Paste connector.

## Tools

| Tool | Widget | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| `pick_paste_item` | picker | Paste `search` |
| `pick_pinboard` | same picker | Paste `list_pinboards` |

Does not create images/files (Paste MCP cannot author those). Does not echo secrets in the picker subtitle.

## Env

See `.env.example`. Do not commit tokens.

## Proposed Paste Cleanup design

### 1. Runtime engine inside `paste-mcp`

Keep cleanup out of `server.ts` handlers. Introduce focused units:

- `cleanup/classify.ts` — pure detectors for secret-shaped content, exact duplicates, misplaced items, malformed titles, stale entries, and board-name drift.
- `cleanup/policy.ts` — maps findings to allowed actions under the active authority tier.
- `cleanup/executor.ts` — typed create/edit/pin/unpin/move/quarantine/delete operations.
- `cleanup/journal.ts` — operation ledger, checkpoints, idempotency keys, and inverse recipes.
- `cleanup/verify.ts` — re-reads Paste and proves each requested postcondition.
- `cleanup/service.ts` — orchestrates opportunistic handling and explicit cleanup jobs.
- Expand `paste-client.ts` with narrowly typed upstream methods; raw Paste responses remain `unknown` until validated.

Processing flow:

```text
Paste result encountered
  → classify locally
  → redact all outward-facing data
  → evaluate policy and authority
  → no-op / enqueue / require approval / execute
  → journal result
  → re-read exact affected item or board
  → record verified, partial, failed, or blocked
```

Opportunistic work must be bounded to items already encountered during normal app operations. An explicit `cleanup_scan` handles broader searches and reports Paste’s search-window limits honestly.

### 2. Authority tiers

| Tier | Authority |
|---|---|
| Observe | Classify, redact, report safe metadata, create cleanup proposals. Automatic. |
| Organize | Create an allowlisted private board; add/remove pins; move by add-destination → verify → remove-source → verify; restore prior membership. May run automatically under an enabled standing policy. |
| Modify | Retitle, edit supported content, rename/merge boards, quarantine duplicates. Requires an approved plan or an explicit standing rule. |
| Destructive | Delete an item or board. Requires exact-target confirmation and Paste’s `confirm: true`; never unattended. |

Shared boards remain read-only unless separately authorized. Images/files may be moved or quarantined but cannot be recreated through Paste MCP.

### 3. Quarantine, deletion, and undo

Default cleanup is quarantine-first using a private `Paste Cleanup — Quarantine` board.

Every operation receives an ID and records:

- item/board IDs, rule ID/version, timestamp, safe classification;
- source/destination memberships and title metadata;
- before/after fingerprints, never secret bodies;
- attempted steps, verified steps, partial failures;
- inverse recipe and whether full undo is technically possible.

Undo uses optimistic preconditions: it refuses to overwrite state changed after cleanup. Moves and retitles are reversible. Hard deletion is explicitly non-undoable for images/files; text/link/color can only be recreated as a new Paste item, not restored with the original identity.

Content edits need a user-approved recovery model. Recommended first release: prohibit automatic body edits, especially for secret-bearing items; support membership and title undo first.

### 4. Dedicated `paste-cleanup` agent

The agent is an operator, not a daemon. Invoke it automatically only when the user asks to audit, organize, clean, undo, or manage Paste; ordinary search/read requests stay with `using-paste-mcp`.

Give it cleanup-specific tools rather than unrestricted raw Paste access:

- `cleanup_scan`
- `cleanup_plan`
- `cleanup_apply`
- `cleanup_undo`
- `cleanup_status`

Tool responses expose IDs, types, classifications, board names, and verification states—not clipboard bodies or secret previews. The runtime engine, not the agent, enforces authority and confirmations.

### 5. `paste-cleanup` skill

The skill should remain a concise operational contract:

```text
scope → scan → classify → preview exact actions → authority check
→ execute permitted actions → verify every target → checkpoint/report
```

Its description should trigger on Paste cleanup, pinboard hygiene, credential organization, duplicate handling, quarantine, deletion, and undo. Detailed classifications and tool schemas belong in a single linked reference, not duplicated in the skill.

Per the latest repository instructions, author the canonical agent/skill at the Tier-0 `~/.Codex` surface first and regenerate/projection-link downstream copies. Avoid maintaining divergent shared and project bodies.

### 6. Thin repository instructions

Add only a routing pointer to `AGENTS.md`, for example:

> For Paste cleanup, credential organization, quarantine, deletion, or undo behavior, read the approved Paste Cleanup design and `paste-cleanup` skill before changing runtime code. Preserve redacted outputs, tiered authorization, journaling, and post-action verification.

Keep tool contracts and rules in the design/skill rather than caching them in `AGENTS.md`.

### 7. Partial failure and verification

Each batch reports totals for `verified`, `partial`, `failed`, `blocked`, and `skipped`. A move that pins successfully but cannot unpin remains a journaled, resumable partial state. Retries apply only to idempotent reads and reversible steps; destructive calls are never blindly retried.

Completion evidence must match the claim:

- action applied → exact target re-read;
- batch complete → every requested target accounted for;
- undo complete → inverse postconditions re-read;
- runtime valid → unit tests plus TypeScript check;
- live integration valid → real Paste test, clearly distinguished from mocks.

### 8. Smallest implementation slices

1. Approve design, terminology, authority matrix, and recovery limits.
2. Add a test runner and fixture-based typed parsing.
3. Build pure classification and policy evaluation with redaction tests.
4. Add append-only journal/checkpoint and idempotency tests.
5. Implement reversible pinboard operations and verification.
6. Add opportunistic observation plus explicit scan/plan/status tools.
7. Add quarantine and undo.
8. Add approval-gated edits and hard deletion.
9. Create the canonical agent, skill, design docs, and thin routing instruction.
10. Run independent security/spec review and live Paste verification.
